name: Toast

hero.title: `toast('Saved')`. From a store, a loader, anywhere.
hero.lede: Mount one `<Toaster />`, then call `toast()` from components, stores, route loaders or a plain `fetch` wrapper. No provider, no hook, no context. Promise toasts, actions, a countdown that waits while the user reads, and the right screen-reader role for each type come with it.

why.title: The toast system you keep rebuilding, finished.

items.title: Call it where the error happens
items.text: A store action, a route loader or an HTTP interceptor can call `toast.error('Card declined')` directly. Error handling stays next to the error, not threaded through a hook.

items.title: Loading to done in one call
items.text: `toast.promise(upload(), { loading: 'Uploading…', success: (n) => `Uploaded ${n} files`, error: 'Upload failed' })` swaps the same toast in place and returns your promise.

items.title: A countdown that waits for the reader
items.text: Hovering, tabbing into a toast, or switching tabs each hold the timer. The holds are tracked separately, so releasing one does not restart the clock while another still holds it.

items.title: Announced with the right urgency
items.text: Errors and warnings use `role="alert"`, info and success `role="status"`, each with `aria-atomic`. The container sets no `aria-live`, so nothing is read twice.

difference.title: You wrote this provider. It never paused on hover.

before.label: React, by hand
before.caption: A context, an array in state, a timer per toast. No pause, no screen-reader role, and no way to call it from outside a component.

after.label: with @pyreon/toast
after.caption: Mount once. Call from anywhere. Pausing, roles, animation and cleanup are done.

comingFrom.title: The calls you know, no React.
comingFrom.note: Same shapes for `promise`, `description` and `action`. sonner's collapsed stack and swipe-to-dismiss are not here; toasts list up to `max` (5 by default).

comingFrom.title: `loading`, then the same id.
comingFrom.note: The same split as react-hot-toast: `toast.dismiss(id)` plays the leave animation, `toast.remove(id)` removes at once.

demo.title: Make some toast.
demo.text: Hover the stack to pause every countdown. The demo's Toaster has `max={3}`: fire more and the newest three stay on screen while older ones wait behind them, coming back when a newer one leaves, unless their own countdown has run out first.

demo.spec: Toaster position top-right, max 3, duration 4000. Buttons fire success, error (with a Retry action), info, a loading toast that `toast.update`s to success after 1.5 s, and `toast.promise` over a 1.5 s promise. Toasts beyond max are not rendered but keep their own timers; when a visible toast is dismissed, the newest hidden one becomes visible. Hovering or focusing the stack pauses all countdowns, hidden toasts included. The built-in Toaster draws no progress bar, so the demo shows none.

features.title: Everything a toast needs, nothing to wire.

items.name: `toast(message, options)`
items.text: Returns an id you can update or dismiss later.

items.name: Presets
items.text: `toast.success`, `.error`, `.warning`, `.info`, and `.loading`, which stays until you update it.

items.name: `toast.promise`
items.text: Loading, then success or error with the result or the error in the message; returns your promise.

items.name: `toast.update(id, …)`
items.text: Change message, type or duration in place, without a new toast.

items.name: Actions
items.text: `{ label: 'Undo', onClick: ({ dismiss }) => … }` with the toast's own dismiss.

items.name: Soft and hard removal
items.text: `dismiss` animates out (200 ms) and fires `onDismiss` once; `remove` is instant.

items.name: Three pause holds
items.text: Hover, keyboard focus and a hidden tab, with the remaining time kept.

items.name: `<Toaster>` props
items.text: `position` (top or bottom; left, center or right), `max`, `gap`, `offset`, `duration`.

recipes.title: Toast every failed request in one place
recipes.text: An interceptor in your HTTP layer, no component involved.

recipes.title: Undo instead of "Are you sure?"
recipes.text: Delete at once, offer Undo for five seconds, and commit only if nobody clicked it.

limits.title: Beyond `max`, older toasts wait unseen
limits.text: The newest `max` toasts (5 by default) are on screen. Older ones keep their own countdown and come back when a newer one leaves, if they have not timed out. Raise `max` or use a dialog for messages that must be read.

limits.title: One position per Toaster
limits.text: `position` is a Toaster prop, so every toast shares it. There is no per-toast position, collapsed stack or swipe-to-dismiss.

limits.title: Mount the Toaster on the client
limits.text: `toast()` on the server is a no-op with a dev warning: a request has no screen to show it on.

limits.title: Native gets the core
limits.text: iOS and Android lower `toast()` and `<Toaster>` with literal options. The native overlay, with description, action and `onDismiss`, lands in the next release. `toast.promise`, `toast.update`, a JSX description and icons stay web and warn by name; the hover pause is web-only. Native targets are experimental.

faq.a: No. The store is a module-level signal. `<Toaster />` renders it through a portal, and `toast()` works from any module once the Toaster is mounted.

faq.q: Where do the speed numbers come from?
faq.a: The toast row of the record: store operations against react-hot-toast 2.5–3.8×, cold creation 3.3× vs react-hot-toast and 2.5× vs sonner, one run under bun. The record also lists a 21–31× DOM-commit figure, measured under happy-dom, so we do not lead with it.
Each toast has the live-region role for its urgency and `aria-atomic`; the stack is a labelled region; keyboard focus pauses the countdown; dismiss and action buttons are real buttons.

faq.q: Can a toast stay until the work finishes?
faq.a: Yes: `toast.loading('Saving…')` has no timeout. `toast.update(id, { type: 'success', message: 'Saved', duration: 4000 })` turns it into a normal toast, or let `toast.promise` do both.

benchmarks.h: From a cold start, toasts go in 3.3× faster than react-hot-toast.
benchmarks.p: Store operations run without a DOM, so they compare the libraries' own work. sonner only removes a dismissed toast after its mounted Toaster animates, so it sits out the headless rows; its Toaster does not render under happy-dom, so it sits out the commit row. It is measured on cold creation. The commit row is happy-dom, a JavaScript DOM: read it as relative.

sources.claim: toast row: headless 2.5–3.8×; cold create 3.3× / 2.5×; happy-dom commit 21–31×; sonner excluded from commit rows
Headless rows vs react-hot-toast only; sonner excluded because dismissal needs a mounted Toaster animation; sonner measured on create
max default 5; Toaster renders the newest max (visibleIds = slice(-max))
Hidden toasts keep their own timers (all five expired after 600 ms headless)
toast.loading has duration 0 (no timeout); toast.update changes type/message in place
toast.promise swaps the same toast and returns the promise; success can be a function of the data
dismiss → state exiting, onDismiss fires once, removed after 200 ms leave
Three independent pause holds (hover, focus, hidden tab)
role alert for error/warning, status for info/success, aria-atomic, container without aria-live
ToastType is info|success|warning|error (loading is a preset, not a type)
Native: toast() + Toaster lower to PyreonToast with literal position/max/gap/offset/duration, description, action, onDismiss, dismiss; promise/update/JSX/icon/pause stay web
Rival code typechecks (sonner 2.0.8, react-hot-toast 2.6.1, React 19 types)
Draft "Toasts beyond max wait in a queue and slide in when space frees up" was wrong: hidden toasts keep counting down
